notes: The hardest case to score: adjacent, not aligned. React and TypeScript transfer directly, but nothing in the CV is mobile, and app store release work is absent entirely. A model that scores this like a React web role is over-crediting transferability; one that scores it like the DevOps mismatch is ignoring it.
jobDescription:
React Native Developer — Consumer App

Our app has 300,000 installs across iOS and Android and we release every two weeks.

What you will do:
- Build features in React Native with TypeScript, using Expo where it fits
- Handle native module integration when Expo does not cover a need
- Own push notifications, deep linking and offline behaviour
- Manage releases through App Store Connect and Google Play, including staged rollout
- Profile and fix performance problems on low-end Android devices

Requirements:
- Demonstrated React Native work, ideally an app you can point to in a store
- Strong React fundamentals and TypeScript
- Understanding of mobile-specific constraints: battery, network, memory
- Familiarity with the mobile release and review process

Nice to have: native iOS or Android experience, experience with analytics and crash reporting tooling.
